title: 3 Questions to Ask Before Buying Off-Plan (Or Walk Away)
seoTitle: 3 Questions to Ask Before Buying Off-Plan
description: Before you sign a presale contract, ask the developer for three things. If they refuse to show you any of them, walk away, no matter how good the brochure is.
answer: Before buying off-plan, ask the developer three things: the real view from your exact unit and from every room, the projects they have already delivered, and the price of similar units in the area with the same layout, quality, floor and orientation. If a developer refuses to show you this, walk away, no matter how beautiful the brochure is.
keywords: questions to ask before buying off-plan
how to check a developer track record
body:
If a developer refuses to show you certain things, walk away from the deal. It does not matter how beautiful the brochure is. When you buy off-plan, you are buying something that does not exist yet, and a brochure is designed to sell, not to inform. These three questions help you see past it.

## 1. What is the view from my exact unit?

Not the view from the penthouse. Not the view from the rooftop in the renderings. You want to know the view from your own unit, and from every window and every room in it.

The view is one of the things you cannot change after you buy. Two units in the same building can have very different views depending on the floor and the orientation. Ask for the view that belongs to the unit you are actually signing for.

## 2. What projects have you already delivered?

A developer's past work is the best evidence of what they will deliver to you. Ask for the list of projects they have completed, then check them yourself:

- Look them up on Google Maps and see what the buildings look like today.
- Better still, visit them in person if you can.
- Compare what was promised with what was built.

A developer who is proud of their past projects will be happy to point you to them.

## 3. What do similar units cost in the area?

The price only makes sense when you compare it. Look for units in the area that are truly similar to yours:

- A similar layout.
- A similar quality of construction and finishes.
- A similar floor.
- A similar orientation.

If you only compare by square footage, you may be comparing very different products. The closer the comparison, the better you can judge whether the price is fair.

## When to walk away

Asking these questions is reasonable. A serious developer should be able to answer all three. If they avoid the questions, change the subject, or send you back to the brochure, treat that as information. A refusal to show you the view, the track record or the comparable prices is a reason to walk away.

This is my view from working in new construction, not financial advice. If you are about to buy your first off-plan property, or you are investing in presales, start with these three questions before you sign anything.
takeaways: If a developer refuses to show you the key information, walk away, no matter how good the brochure is.
Ask for the view from your exact unit and from every room, not the view from the penthouse.
Check the projects the developer already delivered on Google Maps, or visit them in person.
Compare the price with similar units in the area: same layout, quality, floor and orientation.
A serious developer should be able to answer all three questions.
faq: What should I ask a developer before buying off-plan?
Ask for the view from your exact unit, the list of projects they have already delivered, and the prices of similar units in the area. If they will not provide these, walk away.
How do I check a developer's track record?
Ask which projects they have completed, then look them up on Google Maps and, if you can, visit them in person to see the quality of what was actually built.
How do I know if an off-plan price is fair?
Compare it with units in the same area that have a similar layout, quality, floor and orientation. The closer the comparison, the more useful it is.
Is the view in the brochure the view I will get?
Not necessarily. Brochures often show the view from the penthouse or the top floors. Ask for the view from your own unit and from every room in it.
